**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 1.** There is a debate on whether students should be encouraged to learn national/mother tongue languages alongside foreign languages in schools. What is your opinion?
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC série A évalue à la fois le respect du format imposé (essai d'opinion, discours, lettre personnelle) et la qualité du contenu : un texte au contenu riche mais mal formaté perd des points que ni les idées ni la grammaire ne peuvent compenser. Le sujet proposant un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun des trois sujets proposés.

## Topic 1 - Opinion essay: National languages vs foreign languages (modèle, environ 270 mots)

Cameroon is home to more than two hundred national languages, yet French and English, inherited from colonisation, remain the dominant languages of instruction in our schools. This raises an important question: should students be encouraged to learn their national/mother tongues alongside these foreign languages?

I firmly believe they should. First, a language is never simply a tool for communication; it carries the history, proverbs, values and worldview of the community that speaks it. When a national language is abandoned, an entire cultural heritage risks disappearing along with it, especially as younger generations increasingly favour French or English in daily life. Second, research in education consistently shows that children who begin learning in a language they already understand grasp new concepts more easily, which can in turn make it easier, not harder, to later master foreign languages. Third, encouraging national languages fosters a stronger sense of identity and pride among students, rather than the impression that only foreign languages carry prestige or value.

Some argue that time devoted to national languages could instead strengthen French or English, which remain indispensable for national unity and international communication. However, teaching national languages does not have to replace foreign languages; it can complement them, as several pilot programmes already do in Cameroonian schools.

In conclusion, students should indeed be encouraged to learn their national languages, not instead of French and English, but alongside them, so that Cameroon's linguistic and cultural heritage is preserved for future generations while its students remain equipped to engage with the wider world.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 2.** As a youth leader concerned about rising insecurity, give a speech to your community on the importance of vigilance. Your name is Newah Nfor, from Niweh, South West Region.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Speech (modèle, environ 260 mots)

Ladies and gentlemen,

My name is Newah Nfor, and I come to you today from Niweh, in the South West Region, to speak about a matter that affects the safety of every one of us: insecurity, and the vigilance it demands from each citizen.

In recent times, our communities have witnessed a worrying rise in criminal activity: armed robbery, kidnapping, and violent unrest that have left families grieving and businesses destroyed. No security force, however well-equipped, can protect a community whose own members remain passive or indifferent to the warning signs around them.

I therefore call on each of you to embrace three simple habits. First, know your neighbours: a community where people watch out for one another is far harder for criminals to operate in unnoticed. Second, report suspicious activity promptly to the appropriate authorities, rather than assuming someone else will do so. Third, avoid isolated areas after dark whenever possible, and encourage young people in particular to travel in groups.

Vigilance is not about living in fear; it is about living with awareness. A community that looks out for itself is a community that criminals will think twice before targeting.

Ladies and gentlemen, our safety begins with us. Let us each commit, from today, to being active guardians of our own community's peace.

Thank you.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 3.** Write a letter to your grandmother about the dangers of plastic pollution in the village. Your name is Lum Ngwena, from Lookot, East Region, P.O. Box 100.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Formal letter: Plastic pollution (modèle, environ 240 mots)

Lum Ngwena
Lookot
East Region
P.O. Box 100

Dear Grandmother,

I hope this letter finds you in good health. I am writing to share with you a growing concern that has troubled me since my last visit to the village: the amount of plastic waste I noticed scattered around the compound and along the paths near the stream.

I know that plastic bags and bottles are convenient, but they cause serious harm when thrown away carelessly. Unlike organic waste, plastic does not decompose for hundreds of years; instead, it clogs waterways, causing flooding during the rainy season, and it can be swallowed by farm animals with fatal consequences. When burned, it also releases toxic fumes that are harmful to breathe.

I would like to kindly suggest a few simple changes. Perhaps the household could begin separating plastic waste from other rubbish and taking it to a proper collection point rather than burning or dumping it near the stream. Reusable baskets or cloth bags could also replace some of the plastic bags used for shopping at the market.

I share this not to trouble you, but because I care deeply about your health and about the beauty of the village I grew up visiting. I would be glad to help organise a small clean-up with the other grandchildren next time we visit.

With love and respect,

Lum Ngwena

### Piège à éviter
Dans une lettre personnelle (Topic 3), l'erreur fréquente est d'employer par réflexe les formules d'une lettre formelle ("Dear Sir", "Yours faithfully") alors que le destinataire est un proche : le registre doit rester chaleureux et familial du début ("Dear Grandmother") à la fin ("With love").

### Conseil
Avant de rédiger, identifie clairement le destinataire du texte (un ministre, une foule, un proche) : cela détermine immédiatement le registre de langue et les formules d'ouverture/de clôture attendues, bien avant même de réfléchir au contenu.
